messages:
alex: Heads up — dashboard ingest is spiking again. We're hitting per-tenant throttles and CPU on the query layer. Need to decide ownership + whether we split ingest out. Thoughts?

maya: How bad are we talking? any numbers?

alex: Peak ~2.3k req/min from a few tenants. About 10% of requests queue >500ms and we're returning 429s for heavy tenants. Logs show `ingest_queue_len > 2000` during the spike.

rob: Oof. The killer is the per-row RBAC checks we do in the query executor — full policy evals on large projections. That kills throughput. Could push RBAC to the projection layer or precompute an `allowed_bitset` per dashboard.

jess: We have the auth-proxy but it only handles route-level checks. Per-row policies are still in the query. Pushing RBAC out changes correctness assumptions for Private customers (auditing, no-server-assertions).

tony: Quick options:
- A) Precompute projections with auth bitset (fast reads, eventual consistency).
- B) Auth proxy issues tenant-scoped signed tokens to avoid per-row checks.
- C) Keep RBAC in query but optimize hotpaths in native code.
Pros/cons for each re: complexity, privacy, SLO, ops.

alex: Also caching dashboards (30s TTL) cuts load ~40% on similar spikes. Worth considering as an immediate mitigation.

rob: Long-term I'd prefer splitting ingest/transform into a `dashboard-ingest` service that writes projections. Query service becomes read-only projection store. Reduces blast radius and lets us horizontally scale independently.

jess: Migration sketch: shadow writes to projection_v2 for 2 weeks, then canary 10% tenants, feature flag to fallback to v1. Need migration scripts and a short-term compatibility shim. Example flag: `DASH_PROJ_V2_ENABLED=true`

maya: We must keep 95th latency <200ms. If RBAC moves out, tokens must carry exactly-scoped view — can't allow escalation. We'll need thorough threat model + tests.

tony: For Private/VPC installs, token signing must integrate with customer KMS or use server-side session keys. That increases ops work and documentation.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: created INF-824 for `dashboard-ingest` infra. CI pipeline cloned from `events-ingest`, branch: infra/dashboard-ingest.

alex: Action items:
1) Rob & Jess: draft RFC for service split + RBAC refactor by EOW.
2) Maya: perf microbench to quantify per-row RBAC CPU/time (aim: numbers by mid-week).
3) Tony: evaluate KMS/token signing approaches for Private (POC next week).
I'll own rollout and canary plan. :thumbsup:

rob: On it. I'll start RFC skeleton and include migration checklist.

jess: I'll outline compatibility shim and audit requirements.

maya: Starting perf tests now, will post results in this thread.

tony: I'll sync with security on KMS constraints.

alex: Thanks — let's meet Thurs to review RFC draft.

maya: ack

jess: ack

rob: ack

alex: filing follow-up ticket for short-term cache toggle so we can buy time during next spike: INF-825.
